candidate.answerReason: Half the largest disk has area 9π/2. After subtracting the fully shaded inner ring of area 3π, the shaded outer-ring portion has area 3π/2, which is 3/10 of the outer ring. Its central angle is therefore 108°, matching choice A.

methods.label: Find the shaded fraction of the outer ring
methods.explanation:
Equal shaded and unshaded areas mean that the shaded region occupies half the disk inside the largest circle. That disk has area \(\pi\cdot3^2=9\pi\), so the shaded area is \(9\pi/2\).

The fully shaded ring between radii \(1\) and \(2\) has area
\[
\pi\cdot2^2-\pi\cdot1^2=3\pi.
\]
Therefore the shaded portion of the outer ring must have area
\[
\frac{9\pi}{2}-3\pi=\frac{3\pi}{2}.
\]
The entire outer ring, between radii \(2\) and \(3\), has area \(9\pi-4\pi=5\pi\). Its shaded fraction is consequently
\[
\frac{3\pi/2}{5\pi}=\frac{3}{10}.
\]
A sector occupies the same fraction of a circle as its central angle occupies of \(360^\circ\). Subtracting the radius-\(2\) sector from the radius-\(3\) sector preserves that fraction for the ring. Hence
\[
\angle BOC=\frac{3}{10}\cdot360^\circ=108^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{108^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
